items.title: GEO-SEO-Claude: New Tool Optimizes Websites for AI Search Engines
items.summary: Tom Dörr announced a GitHub repository called geo-seo-claude that uses Claude AI to optimize websites specifically for AI search engines. This tool focuses on Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to improve visibility in AI-generated responses. The post garnered over 2,300 likes, highlighting interest in AI-driven SEO innovations.

items.title: Defensive SEO: Protecting Brand Narratives in AI Search
items.summary: Search Engine Land emphasized the shift to defensive SEO as AI summaries influence user perceptions of brands. When asked 'Is [brand] worth it?', AI responses can make or break decisions without clicks to sites. Marketers must monitor and shape these narratives proactively.

items.title: Old SEO vs. New AI SEO: Backlinks to AI Citations
items.summary: Alek Borisov outlined the evolution from traditional SEO (backlinks, rankings, CTR) to AI SEO/GEO/AEO focusing on trusted mentions, AI citations, and structured data. This shift requires new skill sets for visibility in generative answers. The post sparks discussion on adapting strategies.

items.title: Google AI Overviews Slash Search Clicks by 42%
items.summary: A new report reveals Google AI Overviews have reduced organic search clicks by 42%, hitting publishers hard. However, breaking news traffic surged 103% and Discover clicks are booming. SEO pros must adapt to this zero-click trend.

items.title: Prompt Research Emerges as Key SEO and GEO Strategy Layer
items.summary: With AI search going conversational, prompt research uncovers evolving query patterns and content inclusion in AI responses. This technique enhances GEO by aligning content with natural user prompts. Essential for future-proofing SEO.

items.title: Surface-Level SEO Tactics Fail to Secure AI Search Visibility
items.summary: Basic AI SEO advice falls short; lasting visibility demands knowledge graphs, expert entities, and influence in trusted datasets. Oversimplified tactics ignore the complexity of AI engines. Deep strategies are crucial amid evolving search.

items.title: Books on BookTok: Sarah J Maas sends BookTok into 'meltdown'
items.summary: Sarah J. Maas's recent activity or announcement has caused a frenzy on BookTok, sending the community into meltdown. This highlights the influential power of BookTok in driving publishing trends and reader engagement. Publishers continue to track such viral moments for marketing strategies.

items.title: London Book Fair Analysis: Can 'Heated Rivalry' Effect Have Impact?
items.summary: Ahead of London Book Fair, analysis explores how TV adaptations like 'Heated Rivalry' could spark major publishing deals and auctions for related books. Agents predict heated rivalries in bidding if TV success boosts book demand. This reflects growing TV-book synergy in the industry.

items.title: Publishers Using AI to Predict Which Books Will Be Hits
items.summary: Author Ewan Morrison warns that large publishers like Penguin Random House are hiring AI engineers to build forecasting models predicting book performance. This AI will determine which books get purchased and promoted, leading to dark times for creative diversity. The trend stems from internal AI use beyond writing or editing.

items.title: AI Book Scams Boom in Self-Publishing
items.summary: Journalist Fionnuala Mulcahy shares a Guardian story on fraudsters using AI to scam self-publishers with fake marketing and deals. The interactive piece details personalized AI-driven swindles preying on authors' hopes. Highlights the rise of such frauds exploiting the self-publishing surge.

items.title: Guardian Interactive on AI-Supercharged Publishing Fraud
items.summary: Interactive Journalism account promotes Guardian Visuals' piece on AI enabling book swindles targeting self-publishers. Jon's heartbreaking story underscores the fraud boom. Emphasizes need for awareness in the publishing world.

items.title: Viral X Post Details 'Red Flags' for Woke TV and Movie Content
items.summary: Byl Holte enumerates tropes like black characters in medieval Europe, women dominating men physically, and insertions of modern social lectures into fantasy settings that lead him to stop watching shows. The March 5 post receives over 12,000 likes and sparks widespread user comments sharing similar avoidance strategies. It illustrates growing audience selectivity amid perceived forced messaging in entertainment.

items.title: Pop Base Shares Pixar Scrapping Gay Elements from 'Elio'
items.summary: Pixar reportedly cut scenes from 'Elio' implying the protagonist was gay, such as envisioning a family with a male crush. Chief Creative Officer Pete Docter remarked, 'We’re making a movie, not hundreds of millions of dollars of therapy.' The March 7 post garners 18,000 likes, fueling discussions on children's content.

items.title: X Highlights 'Woke Bride' as Latest Hollywood Box Office Failure
items.summary: User shares NewsBusters article on 'The Bride!' bombing with $7.26M opening, labeling it 'Go Woke, Go Broke' for favoring ideology over entertainment. The feminist Frankenstein reinterpretation trails Disney's 'Hoppers' and 'Scream 7'. Posted March 9 amid critiques of agenda-driven flops.

items.title: Woke ‘The Bride!’ Bombs at Box Office: Crushed by ‘Hoppers’ and ‘Scream 7’
items.summary: Warner Bros.' 'The Bride!', directed by Maggie Gyllenhaal with themes of consent and patriarchy critique, opens to $7.26 million on March 9 against a $90 million budget and $16-18M expectations. Disney/Pixar's family animation 'Hoppers' dominates with $46 million while 'Scream 7' earns $17.3 million in week two. Observers point to audience rejection of overt messaging.

items.title: Pixar CCO Pete Docter on Cutting LGBTQ Themes from 'Elio'
items.summary: Pixar removed LGBTQ elements from 'Elio', including a scene of the boy imagining parenthood with a male crush, to prevent forcing unprepared family discussions. Pete Docter stated the studio aims for broad appeal: 'We’re making a movie, not hundreds of millions of dollars of therapy.' Comments from March 7 interview draw activist responses.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Addresses 'Snow White' Casting Backlash
items.summary: Rachel Zegler describes backlash to her 'Snow White' casting as confusing, refusing to 'assimilate for anybody else's comfort' amid criticism of the remake's changes and her political views. She sought therapy after receiving threats. Interview published around March 10 highlights tensions over Disney's live-action updates.

items.title: NEW SBE Council Tech Use Survey: 82% of Small Businesses Now Use AI
items.summary: A new survey shows 82% of small businesses have adopted at least one AI tool, typically using five, resulting in revenue growth for 66%, $243.6 billion in annual time savings, and 81% viewing AI as key to competitiveness. AI is seen as augmenting workers, with 40% of users planning to hire more and 93% intending further investments. Rapid uptake of automated pricing tools (35% using) delivers 97% revenue gains, leveling the field against big firms.

items.title: Small Business Owners Quietly Building Custom AI Tools for Huge Gains
items.summary: Entrepreneurs without coding backgrounds are crafting AI solutions like receptionists saving $4k/month on services, demand forecasters slashing food waste by 40%, style-matching photo editors cutting turnaround from weeks to days and doubling bookings, churn predictors lifting retention 22%, and bespoke CRMs replacing costly software. These practical tools drive efficiency and growth. The divide between AI builders and observers determines business survival.

items.title: AI Reshapes Business Org Structures, Demanding Workflow Redesign
items.summary: AI blurs lines between business, data, product, risk, and ops functions, shifting authority and exposing leadership blind spots in isolated AI hiring. Without integrated operating models linking development, validation, deployment, and accountability, new roles generate activity but not scalable capability. Organizations redesigning work holistically around AI will dominate.

items.title: Microsoft Launches Cloud & AI SMB Partner Resources Collection
items.summary: Microsoft's new asset collection equips partners to seize SMB Cloud and AI growth, featuring decks and guides for Azure migrations, Microsoft Fabric, and AI apps/agents amid SMB operational shifts. Updated March 12, 2026, it emphasizes sales engagement for security, scaling, and innovation plays. This supports small businesses rethinking tech stacks with purpose-built AI solutions.
